summary: This neighbourhood shuts its own streets more than most: for Columbus Day at Sts Peter and Paul, for the annual Blessing of the Fishing Fleet, for the Upper Grant Avenue Street Fair — already in its twenty-ninth year by 1982 — and once for Coit Tower's fiftieth birthday. Through the 1940s the city leased the Crystal Palace Baths on Lombard Street and ran them, and in 1955 it bought land here for a branch library rather than renting a shop as it did in the outer districts. In 1944 a bed factory had Stockton Street closed for ninety days for war work. Telegraph Hill keeps dropping rock onto Sansome Street below it, and the city was still stabilising the slope in 1979.
